title: Scope toggle announces "Exclude: <claim>, pressed" on every in-scope card
body:
## Summary
The whole-card scope toggle flips its accessible NAME with state while also carrying `aria-pressed`, and the two disagree: an in-scope card is announced "Exclude: <claim>, toggle button, pressed" - which a screen-reader user hears as "excluded: on".

## Description
`app/_phases/research/_parts/CardTile.tsx:304-305`: `aria-pressed={!s.descoped}` (pressed = in scope) and `aria-label={`${s.descoped ? "Include" : "Exclude"}: ${card.title}`}`. When the card is in scope, pressed=true and the name is the verb for the OTHER state. A toggle button's name must name the thing that is on when pressed (ARIA APG: a toggle's label does not change with its state). The descoped branch ("Include: X, not pressed") happens to read coherently; the in-scope branch - the DEFAULT for 28 of the 36 cards - is inverted. The file header (CardTile.tsx:13-28) records that this overlay was built precisely so a screen reader gets the scope state right; the state it gets is backwards.
Sibling: `CardActions.tsx:89,104` also swaps names with state ("Like:"/"Liked:", "Deepen:"/"Queued for deeper research:") on top of `aria-pressed` - not contradictory, but double-announced ("Liked: X, pressed"). Same fix shape, same commit.

## Flow
- Screen-reader user opens the expert face and Tabs into a column.
- Hears "Exclude: <claim>, toggle button, pressed".
- Concludes the card is excluded; presses to "include" it - and descopes it.

## Expected impact
The one decision this board exists for is announced inverted for every untouched card; a non-sighted creator cuts what they meant to keep.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a screen-reader user hears the true scope state of each card.
Before: 28/36 cards (non-required, non-opt-in, in scope by default) announce "Exclude: ..., pressed"; every taken conclusion does too.
After: 0 - stable names "In scope: <claim>" / "Like: <claim>" / "Deepen: <claim>", state carried by aria-pressed alone.
Method: probe - counted via buildCards() (36 total, 1 required, 7 opt-in -> 28); the name/state pairing read off CardTile.tsx:304-305.
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: app/_phases/research/_parts/CardTile.tsx:304 aria-pressed={!s.descoped}; :305 aria-label={`${s.descoped ? "Include" : "Exclude"}: ${card.title}`}; app/_phases/research/_parts/CardActions.tsx:89 name={s.liked ? `Liked: ...` : `Like: ...`}; :104 name={s.deepen ? `Queued for deeper research: ...` : `Deepen: ...`}. npx tsx over buildCards(): {total:36, required:1, optIn:7, inScopeByDefaultToggles:28}. grep 'Include: |Exclude: |Like: |Deepen: ' tests -> 0 hits (no test pins the old names).
verify: New probe tests/golden-path/scope-toggle-name.probe.spec.ts: read CardTile.tsx and CardActions.tsx, stripComments (tests/golden-path/_helpers.ts), assert (a) the scope-toggle aria-label expression has no ternary on `s.descoped` (regex /aria-label=\{`\$\{s\.descoped \?/ absent), (b) CardActions' `name=` props have no ternary on `s.liked`/`s.deepen` (regex /name=\{s\.(liked|deepen) \?/ absent), (c) `aria-pressed` still present on all three. Red on HEAD (3 matches), green after. Then npm run typecheck.

title: Music-video attach: a storage failure after decode reads as "decoding…" forever
body:
## Summary
`attach` guards only the decode. The three storage writes after it are unguarded, so a failed upload renders exactly like an upload in progress (forever), and a failed save renders exactly like success.

## Description
`app/_phases/research/useMusicVideoSource.ts:105-115` wraps `analyzeAudioEnvelope` in try/catch and sets `status:"error"`. Lines 117-124 then run `await putUploads([pair])`, `await write(...)`, `await markResearched()` with no guard:
- `putUploads` (lib/assets.ts:348-363) has try/finally and NO catch - an IndexedDB quota/blocked/unavailable error rejects. `status` was set to "decoding" at :100 and is never reset, so `MusicVideoResearch.tsx:44-48` keeps `role=status` "decoding <file>…" up indefinitely, the rejection escapes Dropzone's `onFiles` as an unhandled rejection, and nothing on the surface says the attach failed. FAILURE == NEVER-RETURNS.
- `saveStep` does not throw - it RETURNS `{ok:false, trouble}` (stepStore.ts:293-296, :648). `write` (:59-67) and `markResearched` (:73-81) discard that outcome. `setEnvelope(env)` already ran at :121, so a failed save draws the tempo tallies and `usePhaseReport` reports "done" (MusicVideoResearch.tsx:26) while neither the envelope nor `researched:true` reached disk - Script's gate (the record markResearched exists to write, per the hook header :8-22) stays shut behind a Research step that says it is finished. FAILURE == SUCCESS.
The sibling pattern exists: `frames/music-video/EffectsStudio.tsx:136` branches on `outcome.ok`.
Also: `clearError` (:129-132) has zero consumers.

## Flow
- Creator drops an mp3 in a browser whose storage is full / blocked.
- Decode succeeds; putUploads rejects -> "decoding track.mp3…" never clears. Or: putUploads succeeds, saveStep returns ok:false -> tallies + shelf "done", Script still blocked after reload.

## Expected impact
The music-video discipline's only Research act can strand the creator with no error and no retry signal, and the step contradicts the bell's storage-failure report.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - an attach that did not persist says so on the surface that started it.
Before: 3 awaited persistence calls in `attach` outside any try/outcome check (putUploads, write, markResearched); failure-after-decode renders identical to in-flight; save failure renders identical to success.
After: 0 unguarded - putUploads inside try/catch -> status "error" with a message naming the file; write/markResearched return SaveOutcome and !ok sets status "error"; setEnvelope only after persistence succeeds.
Method: probe - read off useMusicVideoSource.ts:95-127 and the putUploads/saveStep signatures; a source ratchet holds it.
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: app/_phases/research/useMusicVideoSource.ts:100 setStatus("decoding"); :105-115 try covers analyzeAudioEnvelope only; :118 await putUploads([pair]) unguarded; :121 setEnvelope(env) BEFORE persistence; :123-124 await write(...)/markResearched() outcome discarded; :59-67 write returns void. lib/assets.ts:351-362 try/finally, no catch. app/_phases/_shared/stepStore.ts:293-296 SaveOutcome {ok:false,trouble}; :648 `if (!r.ok) return r`. app/_phases/research/MusicVideoResearch.tsx:26 phase report "done" off mv.envelope; :44-48 decoding status. grep clearError app -> only its definition (useMusicVideoSource.ts:129,144). Sibling: app/_phases/frames/music-video/EffectsStudio.tsx:136 `if (outcome.ok)`.
verify:
New probe tests/golden-path/music-video-attach-failure.probe.spec.ts: stripComments(useMusicVideoSource.ts), slice the `attach` useCallback body, assert (a) `await putUploads(` sits inside a `try {` whose `catch` contains `setStatus("error")`, (b) `write` and `markResearched` return their saveStep outcome and attach checks `.ok`, (c) `setEnvelope(` appears AFTER the persistence awaits. Red on HEAD, green after. Either wire clearError to a dismiss on the role=alert

or delete it. npm run typecheck + npm run lint:ratchet.

title: Music-video Dropzone draws no frame and no glyph inside the studio
body:
## Summary The kit Dropzone paints its dashed frame, hover tint and plate glyph from `--al-gold`, which is declared only under `[data-world=...]`. The studio's obsidian StudioFrame sets no `data-world`, so on the Research step the drop target renders as one line of constraint text in an invisible 34px-padded box. ## Description - `components/kit/kit.css:607-608` `.k-drop { border: 1px dashed color-mix(in srgb, var(--al-gold) 45%, transparent) ... }`, hover `background/border-color: var(--al-gold)`; `components/kit/Dropzone.tsx` svg `style={{ stroke: "var(--al-gold)" }}`. - `--al-gold` exists only in `[data-world="almanac"]{...}[data-world="obsidian"]{...}` (components/ui/tokens.ts:335; WORLD_ALMANAC :242, WORLD_OBSIDIAN_KIT :287). `:root` does not declare it. - `app/studio/[projectId]/StudioView.tsx:282` mounts `` with the default `world="obsidian"` (StudioFrame.tsx:66), whose branch (:141) is a plain div with no `data-world`; only the almanac branch wraps in `WorldRoot`. - An undefined custom property with no fallback makes the `border` declaration invalid at computed-value time -> border-style none; `stroke` falls back to inherited `none`. Two of the Dropzone's three drawn parts vanish; only `

{constraints}

` survives. PAIR: the other two Dropzone consumers (app/library/audio/Inspector.tsx:770, References.tsx:138) render inside `AudioWorkbench.tsx:553 `, where `--al-gold` resolves to `--gt-accent-cyan` - same component, frame visible there, absent here. The Ghost-at-0.12 class of defect: every gate green, only a photograph shows it. ## Flow - Open a music-video project's Research step. - See "mp3 · wav · m4a — one track, analyzed once on drop" floating with no target, no plate, no hover response. ## Expected impact The single action of this discipline's Research step has no visible affordance. ## Evaluation Claim: user - the drop target is visible where it is used. Before: inside /studio/?step=research (music-video): `--al-gold` undeclared on every ancestor -> 0 of {frame, glyph, hover tint} drawn. After: wrap the Dropzone in `
` (MusicVideoResearch.tsx:35) -> `--al-gold` = var(--gt-accent-cyan), all 3 drawn, matching the Library audio twin. (Kit-wide alternative - StudioFrame's obsidian root declaring data-world="obsidian" - is a Lane B call; this is the in-context fix.) Method: probe - token scoping read off tokens.ts:335 + StudioFrame.tsx:66/:141 + kit.css:607; confirm with a cx-capture photo. Result: better Gate: none
evidence: components/ui/tokens.ts:335 returns `:root{decls}[data-world="almanac"]{world}[data-world="obsidian"]{obsidianKit}`; grep '--al-gold' over *.css/*.ts -> only tokens.ts:242 (WORLD_ALMANAC) and :287 (WORLD_OBSIDIAN_KIT). components/ui/StudioFrame.tsx:66 world="obsidian" default; :102-131 only the almanac branch uses WorldRoot; :141 obsidian root div has no data-world. app/studio/[projectId]/StudioView.tsx:282 `<StudioFrame>`. components/kit/kit.css:607-609 .k-drop rules on var(--al-gold). app/_phases/research/MusicVideoResearch.tsx:35-41 Dropzone with no world ancestor. Twin: app/library/audio/AudioWorkbench.tsx:553 `<WorldRoot world="obsidian" className="ab-world">` wraps the Inspector.tsx:770 / References.tsx:138 Dropzones.
verify: Probe tests/golden-path/music-video-dropzone-world.probe.spec.ts: stripComments(MusicVideoResearch.tsx) and assert an element carrying `data-world="obsidian"` opens before `<Dropzone` and closes after it (red on HEAD: 0 occurrences). Then photograph: NEXT_PUBLIC_DEV_AUTH=1 NEXT_DIST_DIR=.next-cx npx next dev -p 3007, open a music-video project, CX_BASE=http://localhost:3007 CX_PROJECT=<id> node pipeline/cx-capture.mjs studio-research out.png --width 1920 - the dashed cyan frame and plate must be visible.

title: Dropzone has no keyboard path: music-video research needs a mouse
body:
## Summary
The kit Dropzone is a `<div onClick>` with no role, no tabIndex and no key handler, wrapping a `hidden` file input. On the music-video discipline it is the ONLY way to do Research, so keyboard and switch users hit a dead end at Step 1.

## Description
`components/kit/Dropzone.tsx:28-43`: root `<div onClick={() => input.current?.click()} aria-label={label} className="k-drop">`; `<input type="file" ... hidden>` (:44) - `hidden` removes the input from the tab order and the a11y tree. No `role`, no `tabIndex`, no `onKeyDown`. `aria-label` on a generic div is prohibited (ARIA 1.2) and ignored by most AT, so the header's claim (:4-5 "The frame carries its accessible name for anyone who cannot see the dashes") is false in practice - a docstring promising what the JSX does not deliver.
Consumer in this context: `app/_phases/research/MusicVideoResearch.tsx:35-41`, the step's sole action (ResearchStep.tsx:111 routes every music-video project here). Also `multiple` is set while `useMusicVideoSource.ts:97` takes `files[0]` - a second file is silently dropped.
Fix lives in components/kit (3 consumers: MusicVideoResearch, library/audio/Inspector.tsx:770, References.tsx:138), so Lane B: e.g. make the root a `<label>` around a visually-hidden (sr-only, not `hidden`) input, or a `<button type=button>` that clicks the input, with a focus-visible ring; add `multiple?: boolean` defaulting to false.

## Flow
- Keyboard user opens a music-video project's Research step.
- Tab skips the drop target entirely (only the style input is focusable).
- No way to attach the track; Script stays gated on research.

## Expected impact
A whole discipline is unusable without a pointer.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a keyboard user can attach the track.
Before: 0 focusable elements leading to the file picker on the music-video Research surface (root not focusable; input `hidden`); 3 kit consumers affected.
After: 1 focusable, named control per Dropzone; Enter/Space opens the picker.
Method: probe - read off Dropzone.tsx:28-45.
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: components/kit/Dropzone.tsx:28-43 `<div onDragOver.. onDrop.. onClick={() => input.current?.click()} data-testid={testId} aria-label={label} className=...>` - no role/tabIndex/onKeyDown; :44 `<input ref={input} type="file" accept={accept} multiple hidden ...>`; header :4-5 claims an accessible name. Consumers (grep Dropzone app): app/_phases/research/MusicVideoResearch.tsx:35, app/library/audio/Inspector.tsx:770, app/library/audio/References.tsx:138 (+ app/kit/Parts.tsx demo). app/_phases/research/useMusicVideoSource.ts:97 uses files[0] only. app/_phases/research/ResearchStep.tsx:111 music-video -> MusicVideoResearch.
verify: Probe tests/golden-path/dropzone-keyboard.probe.spec.ts: stripComments(components/kit/Dropzone.tsx) and assert the file input is not `hidden` (sr-only instead) AND the root is a <label> or <button> (or carries role="button" + tabIndex={0} + onKeyDown) - red on HEAD. Then a browser check: Tab on a music-video Research step reaches the dropzone and Enter opens the file chooser (Playwright page.waitForEvent('filechooser')).

title: Attached track can never be replaced, and after reload it is never named
body:
## Summary
Once a track decodes, `MusicVideoResearch` removes the Dropzone and offers no other route to a different track. The hook's own docstring plans for a re-attach the surface cannot reach, and the attached file's name is session-only, so after a reload the step shows six numbers and nothing saying WHICH track they describe.

## Description
- `MusicVideoResearch.tsx:34` `{!mv.envelope && <Dropzone .../>}` - with an envelope stored there is no attach, replace or clear control on the step (the style input is the only other control).
- `useMusicVideoSource.ts:69-72`: markResearched "Reads the existing record first so a project ... (the same discipline against a re-attach) does not lose it" - a spec for re-attach the JSX makes unreachable.
- `fileName` (:46) is set only in `attach` (:102) and is not part of `MusicVideoSourceStepData` (stepStore.ts:233-249), so after reload `MusicVideoResearch.tsx:61-74` draws duration/frames/fps/tempo tallies with no track identity. The name is recoverable from `sourceAssetId` (the Asset record) without a schema change.
- A creator who dropped the wrong mp3 has no way back short of a new project.
Why Lane B: replacing the track must decide what happens to the WP3 fields keyed to the old envelope (`posterAssetId`, `seed`, `effectParams` - stepStore.ts:241-247; `write` merges `{...current, ...patch}`, so they would silently survive against a different song) and to Frames work already done. That is a cross-step contract call, not a drawing change.

## Flow
- Drop a track; realise it is the wrong edit.
- The Dropzone is gone; nothing on Research offers a replacement.
- Reload: tallies only, no filename.

## Expected impact
An irreversible-by-accident choice on the discipline's only Research act, and a summary the creator cannot check against their own files.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the creator can see which track is attached and swap it.
Before: 0 replace routes once `envelope` exists; 0 track names rendered after reload (fileName not persisted).
After: 1 replace route (compact Dropzone / "replace track" when an envelope exists) + the attached asset's name from sourceAssetId; replacement clears or flags the WP3 fields.
Method: simulation - walked MusicVideoResearch.tsx:34-75 and the useMusicVideoSource state lifecycle; downstream reconciliation not measured.
Result: better
Gate: contract
evidence: app/_phases/research/MusicVideoResearch.tsx:34 `{!mv.envelope && (<Dropzone`; :61-74 tallies only, no name. app/_phases/research/useMusicVideoSource.ts:46 fileName useState (session-only), :102 setFileName only in attach, :50-54 hydration restores no name, :69-72 docstring 'against a re-attach'; :64 write merges {...current, ...patch}. app/_phases/_shared/stepStore.ts:233-249 MusicVideoSourceStepData has no name field; :241-247 WP3 fields posterAssetId/seed/effectParams.
verify: Probe: stripComments(MusicVideoResearch.tsx) asserts a Dropzone (or replace control) renders in the `mv.envelope` branch and a name derived from sourceAssetId renders beside the tallies - red on HEAD. Plus a recorded decision on what a re-attach does to posterAssetId/seed/effectParams (clear vs keep-with-stale-flag), held by a unit over the merge in `attach`.

lens_checked.ux-reviewer: Walked ResearchStep.tsx discipline branch (opening / no-project / educational / music-video / beats), ExpertBoard empty state -> expert-board-start, ClearDialog destination (doClear -> guided), ModeChooser/ModeSwitch reversibility, BeatVariantBoard compose/reopen, FollowUpQueue run/busy, music-video attach lifecycle (finding 5). Not emitted: ModeSwitch's locked reason lives only in `title` on a DISABLED button (ModeChooser.tsx:122-123, string at ResearchStep.tsx:162) - unreachable by keyboard; a <Hint> beside it is the shape.
lens_checked.state-coverage: Per data source: getProject null/undefined/value (ResearchStep.tsx:90-97); useBeatPicks hydrated gate (:146, BeatVariantBoard.tsx:37); useScope + face hydration (:215); triage columns empty vs none-kept vs orphan (ResearchTriageBoard.tsx:204-236); FollowUpQueue zero rows (Ghost) vs settled-job-no-rows Notice (:213-247) vs unanswered (:286); music-video hydrated/decoding/error/envelope (finding 2).

Not emitted: the broken state has three spellings - ScopeBar.tsx:21 'wounded', ScopeBar.tsx:102 'cannot be argued', CardTile.tsx:235 'cannot stand —'. CardTile.tsx:135 hottest-take title= restates the visible CardTile.tsx:167 'speculation about motive — not reporting' and is 1 of 3 in-context entries (with CardActions.tsx:91,105) in check:narration's 5-title budget (node pipeline/check-narration.mjs -> 5/5); deleting it is a free ratchet step. ClearDialog 'six searches' and the notebook modal title match the static shared notebook (scope.ts buildCards is static), so they are consistent with what renders.

FollowUpQueue.tsx:195-202 question input is named only by its placeholder - weak but computed by accname.
